messages:
jamie: heads-up — hit a flaky rollback last night after a tiny policy tweak. it wasn't catastrophic but calls started hedging to cheaper models unexpectedly. thinking we need a sim-driven preflight harness that reproducibly exercises policy deltas before rollout. goals: deterministic traffic replay, seedable randomness, cache warm/cold scenarios, time-of-day cost curves, and injected region blackouts. thoughts?

sam: love this. +1 on deterministic replay. also add tenant budget envelopes and request-rate throttles so we catch starvation. output should include switching-rate, latency delta distribution, and cost-per-1k delta.

maria: re: cost curves — we need to standardize how we represent cost over time (linear vs step vs noisy). sim should accept a small DSL for cost signals so we can mock promos/spot-price spikes. also store policy snapshots with fixed ids for audits.

olivia: implementation idea: make policy-sim a small library that can import the policy graph (json proto), run a deterministic evaluator, and replay sanitized traces from prod. CLI prototype: ```rwd-policy-sim run --replay traces/2026-03-20.json --seed 42 --cache-warm 0.1 --inject-region us-east-1:0.2 --cost-signal cost.yaml --out sim-20260320.json``` This should produce a compact delta-report with per-tenant diffs.

jamie: +1. also need to exercise KV cache states (cold start vs warmed) — the same policy can behave differently if prefix cache is present. can we simulate prefix cache hit rates?

sam: yes, add `--cache-warm` and `--kv-hit-profile` flags. recommend a small set of canonical profiles: cold, steady, high-locality.

maria: curious about runtime parity: sim must use the exact kernel/adapter selection logic or we'll miss regressions. maybe extract a thin evaluator from runtime (no GPUs) that mirrors decision points. that is heavier but safer.

olivia: agreed. keep the evaluator small and well-tested. for faster loops use sample traces and a "fast-mode" that approximates latency instead of running full kernels. full fidelity runs can be nightly.

policy-sim-bot: sim-run-id=sim-20260320-42 | switching-rate=3.4% | median-latency=+12ms | p95-latency=+60ms | cost-per-1k=+$0.23 | issues: route oscillation detected for tenant:alpha when budget<5% (repro-id=osc-771)

jamie: ok this output is exactly the kind of thing we need. can we also surface stability heatmaps (time vs switching-rate) and top-k request fingerprints that triggered flips?

sam: yep — sim should emit small artifacts: heatmap png, delta csv, and a culprit sample set (n=20) with request payloads redacted. include a reproducible command to re-run just the culprit set.

maria: ops question — where do we run heavy sims? nightly in a dedicated infra project or on-demand in CI workers with capped runtime? my vote: nightly full-fidelity runs + pre-merge fast checks. also gate canary rollouts on sim pass/fail thresholds.

olivia: I can wire a minimal POC into rollout UI: attach sim-run summary to each policy change so reviewers can eyeball switching-rate and cost. quick UX: show green if switching-rate<1% and p95-latency delta<10ms or cost delta<+$0.10/1k. configable per-tenant.

jamie: who wants to be owner for prototyping RFC + implementation plan? I'll write the RFC draft if someone pairs on a prototype.

sam: I can prototype the evaluator and replay harness this sprint. will mock cost DSL and kv profiles.

maria: I'll help with integration tests and define the sim-to-runtime parity checklist.

olivia: I'll add the CLI UX and a basic rollout UI attachment.

jamie: awesome. i'll start the RFC and include: sim design, artifacts, gating criteria, perf cost, and rollout plan + escalation playbook. ping me on this thread with links and small PRs. :thumbsup:

sam: cool, filing a quick tracker ticket and will drop traces + toy cost yaml here for initial runs.

policy-sim-bot: note: remember to scrub PII from traces. use `rwd-scrub --level=high`. recommended fields to remove: user IDs, email, prompt content if private.

jamie: noted. thanks everyone — moving to RFC draft now.
